finding: Five Hosted Linux PR-layer tests exposed version-dependent behavior: stdlib JSON parsing raised RecursionError for deeply nested JSON on one runtime, while other readers reached generic schema errors or accepted the same shape. Existing RecursionError normalization alone did not provide a stable cross-platform boundary.
fix: Add a shared rles_contracts.json_utils.ensure_json_nesting_depth scanner with a 512-container limit. It ignores quoted and escaped delimiters. Apply it before parsing in all seven package strict JSON helpers, Binance transfer single/page importers, rles-data manifest CLI, orchestrator legacy inventory reader, Research ArtifactStore integrity/completion/L1 manifests, contract error and canonical-byte readers, and compute worker transport serialization/decode boundaries. The hosted follow-on exposed one additional QA reader: qa/world_model/reconcile_routeb_research_ledger.py now preflights canonical report JSON with the same shared guard.
assertions: All seven package strict readers reject over-limit input before platform-dependent JSON parsing.
Binance single and paged imports preserve MetricsError boundary on over-depth documents.
The data CLI returns the stable nesting-depth DataError instead of a generic schema error.
The legacy inventory reader returns the stable nesting-depth DataError.
Research ArtifactStore integrity, completion, and L1 manifests reject excessive depth within ArtifactError boundary.
Contract error/canonical readers and compute transport map excess depth to their public error boundary.
Quoted delimiters and escaped quotes do not count toward structural nesting; depth 512 is accepted and 513 rejected.
The RouteB research-ledger reconciler rejects excessive nesting inside its canonical-report JSON error boundary.
